commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

1	# Results: formulation T on the seven instances
2	
3	All seven MIPs reached the 0.01% gap well inside the 600 s limit, and all seven LP relaxations solved to optimality.
4	
5	The model departs from the paper's printed text in a few places. One of them, the renewable term in the reserve row (67), changes the objective by up to 135%. See [Effect of the reserve equation](#effect-of-the-reserve-equation) and `NOTES.md`.
6	
7	## Main results
8	
9	Objectives are in dollars. Times are Gurobi's reported runtime and exclude reading the file and building the model. "Root gap" is (MIP objective − LP objective) / MIP objective.
10	
11	| Instance | LP objective | LP time (s) | MIP objective | MIP bound | Gap | MIP time (s) | Nodes | Status | Root gap |
12	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
13	| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 0.60 | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 0.0055% | 40.75 | 20366 | OPTIMAL | 0.31% |
14	| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 0.38 | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 0.0099% | 4.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.18% |
15	| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2697031.224634 | 0.52 | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 0.0092% | 8.79 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.39% |
16	| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 6.30 | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 0.0096% | 20.86 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
17	| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 6.10 | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 0.0100% | 25.53 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
18	| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 26.02 | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 0.0018% | 54.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
19	| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 21.64 | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 0.0026% | 58.75 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
20	
21	OPTIMAL here means within the 0.01% gap, not proved exactly optimal.
22	
23	Load shed, over-generation and reserve shortfall were zero in every MIP and LP solution above.
24	
25	| Instance | Renewable used (MWh) | Available (MWh) | Variables | Binaries | Constraints | Nonzeros |
26	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
27	| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 127873.596 | 148361.000 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
28	| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 78694.790 | 78711.600 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
29	| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 80719.254 | 86297.500 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
30	| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0.000 | 0.000 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
31	| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 647317.506 | 647317.506 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
32	| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 1989211.583 | 2106677.220 | 371631 | 181359 | 506007 | 2298488 |
33	| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 123146.177 | 123146.177 | 378916 | 187252 | 536643 | 2375635 |
34	
35	Solution files are in `results/`: `<instance>.mip.csv` and `<instance>.lp.csv`. In an LP file, `on` is `u` rounded to 0 or 1 while `power` and `available` use the fractional `u`.
36	
37	### Setup
38	
39	- Gurobi 13.0.2, with defaults except `MIPGap=0.0001` and `TimeLimit=600`.
40	- AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8 cores and 16 threads, 14 GB of RAM. Gurobi used up to 16 threads.
41	- The solves ran one at a time, with no other solver running.
42	
43	The commands, for each instance, were:
44	
45	```
46	build/uc_solve --relax --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.lp.csv data/NAME.json
47	build/uc_solve --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.mip.csv --log results/NAME.mip.log data/NAME.json
48	```
49	
50	The `.mip.log` files were appended to by more than one run, so each holds several solves. Runs of the same model gave the same objective, bound and node count. The LP `.lp.log` files come from an earlier pass that gave the same objectives.
51	
52	The binary changed once after these runs, and only in how it prints a bound that is still infinite. `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` was rerun on the last binary as a check.
53	
54	## Comparison with the paper
55	
56	The paper reports no objective values, so only solve times can be compared. Its T times come from supplement Tables 17 to 19, on Gurobi 8.0.1 and a Xeon E5-2670. A different solver version and machine make the absolute times incomparable.
57	
58	| Instance | Paper's name for it | Paper T (s) | This work (s) |
59	|---|---|---:|---:|
60	| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2020-01-27 CP | 88.8 | 40.75 |
61	| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 2020-07-06 CP | 6.8 | 4.46 |
62	| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2020-12-23 CP | 19.4 | 8.79 |
63	| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 2014-09-01 3% | 83.5 | 20.86 |
64	| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | Scenario400 1% | 66.5 | 25.53 |
65	| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 2015-01-01 HW | 210.4 | 54.46 |
66	| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 2015-04-01 LW | 411.6 | 58.75 |
67	
68	## Effect of the reserve equation
69	
70	This is the decision that matters most. Equation (67) as printed has no renewable term, so thermal capacity alone must cover load plus reserve. The default model adds the renewable output to the left side. `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.
71	
72	| Instance | LP, as printed | MIP, as printed | MIP bound | Time (s) | Nodes | MIP change from default |
73	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
74	| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2886327.663320 | 2895818.506145 | 2895818.506145 | 5.11 | 1 | +135.3% |
75	| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 4738304.251865 | 4744049.174369 | 4743596.078260 | 118.32 | 57703 | +27.2% |
76	| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 3420212.426006 | 3427596.725367 | 3427511.589515 | 6.67 | 1 | +26.6% |
77	| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48408.252585 | 48404.447154 | 19.46 | 1 | none (no renewables) |
78	| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 59131.628059 | 59294.766885 | 59289.559388 | 96.74 | 1959 | +76.5% |
79	| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 70787813.609122 | 70853552.802373 | 70846642.488301 | 77.85 | 1 | +70.8% |
80	| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57415416.765581 | 57424327.867364 | 57422963.483430 | 103.42 | 1 | +0.7% |
81	
82	All of these reached the 0.01% gap. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, the printed form uses only 57746 of the 148361 MWh of renewable energy (61% curtailed, against 14% by default), with no reserve shortfall: it curtails free energy to keep thermal units committed.
83	
84	## Checks
85	
86	The objective of each solution was not recomputed by separate code. The tools written for that could not be run in this environment; see "Verification" in `NOTES.md`.
87	
88	**Comparison with an unstrengthened model.** `--variant base` replaces T's generation limits, ramping and piecewise bounds with the basic physical constraints (18), (19), (24), (25), (42). It has the same integer feasible set if T's strengthening is valid, so each model's objective should lie above the other's bound.
89	
90	| Instance | T objective | T bound | Base objective | Base bound | Consistent |
91	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
92	| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 1230475.366858 | 1230372.814177 | yes |
93	| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 3729194.920899 | 3728823.125816 | yes |
94	| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 2707458.250828 | 2707196.479605 | yes |
95	| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 48407.906437 | 48404.148645 | yes |
96	| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 33590.159078 | 33587.075872 | yes |
97	| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 41483616.907983 | 41482325.156730 | yes |
98	| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 57004338.160063 | 56999545.483832 | yes |
99	
100	This test has limits. It cannot see an error smaller than the gap, which is about $300 on the RTS instances and $5000 on FERC. The two models also share the objective, the up/down-time rows and the start-up rows, so it says nothing about errors in those.
101	
102	**Hand checks on `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06`, period 18.**
103	- Thermal output 4861.93 MW plus renewable 1269.30 MW equals demand 6131.23 MW.
104	- Headroom on the units with spare capacity sums to 183.9369 MW, which equals the reserve requirement.
105	- Unit `101_STEAM_3` starts at 30 MW with `RU`=`RD`=40. Its `p(1)`=70 is exactly `p0+RU`, and its availability at t=9 is exactly `p(8)+RU`. Its largest drop, 28.71 MW, is within `RD`.
106	
107	**File format.** On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the MIP CSV has 74 rows for period 1: 73 generators and `RENEWABLE`.
108	
109	**Independent review.** A separate agent compared `src/model.c` and `src/instance.c` with the paper by reading and hand derivation, without running anything. It found no defect in the default model, and its hand examples support each departure from the printed text.
110	
111	**Command line.** A 1 s limit on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` returned status `TIME_LIMIT`, an incumbent and `bound=-inf`. A non-JSON input gave a parse error and exit code 1.
112

# Results: formulation T on the seven instances

All seven MIPs reached the 0.01% gap well inside the 600 s limit, and all seven LP relaxations solved to optimality.

The model departs from the paper's printed text in a few places. One of them, the renewable term in the reserve row (67), changes the objective by up to 135%. See [Effect of the reserve equation](#effect-of-the-reserve-equation) and `NOTES.md`.

## Main results

Objectives are in dollars. Times are Gurobi's reported runtime and exclude reading the file and building the model. "Root gap" is (MIP objective − LP objective) / MIP objective.

| Instance | LP objective | LP time (s) | MIP objective | MIP bound | Gap | MIP time (s) | Nodes | Status | Root gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 0.60 | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 0.0055% | 40.75 | 20366 | OPTIMAL | 0.31% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 0.38 | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 0.0099% | 4.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.18% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2697031.224634 | 0.52 | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 0.0092% | 8.79 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.39% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 6.30 | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 0.0096% | 20.86 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 6.10 | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 0.0100% | 25.53 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 26.02 | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 0.0018% | 54.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 21.64 | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 0.0026% | 58.75 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |

OPTIMAL here means within the 0.01% gap, not proved exactly optimal.

Load shed, over-generation and reserve shortfall were zero in every MIP and LP solution above.

| Instance | Renewable used (MWh) | Available (MWh) | Variables | Binaries | Constraints | Nonzeros |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 127873.596 | 148361.000 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 78694.790 | 78711.600 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 80719.254 | 86297.500 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0.000 | 0.000 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 647317.506 | 647317.506 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 1989211.583 | 2106677.220 | 371631 | 181359 | 506007 | 2298488 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 123146.177 | 123146.177 | 378916 | 187252 | 536643 | 2375635 |

Solution files are in `results/`: `<instance>.mip.csv` and `<instance>.lp.csv`. In an LP file, `on` is `u` rounded to 0 or 1 while `power` and `available` use the fractional `u`.

### Setup

- Gurobi 13.0.2, with defaults except `MIPGap=0.0001` and `TimeLimit=600`.
- AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8 cores and 16 threads, 14 GB of RAM. Gurobi used up to 16 threads.
- The solves ran one at a time, with no other solver running.

The commands, for each instance, were:

```
build/uc_solve --relax --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.lp.csv data/NAME.json
build/uc_solve --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.mip.csv --log results/NAME.mip.log data/NAME.json
```

The `.mip.log` files were appended to by more than one run, so each holds several solves. Runs of the same model gave the same objective, bound and node count. The LP `.lp.log` files come from an earlier pass that gave the same objectives.

The binary changed once after these runs, and only in how it prints a bound that is still infinite. `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` was rerun on the last binary as a check.

## Comparison with the paper

The paper reports no objective values, so only solve times can be compared. Its T times come from supplement Tables 17 to 19, on Gurobi 8.0.1 and a Xeon E5-2670. A different solver version and machine make the absolute times incomparable.

| Instance | Paper's name for it | Paper T (s) | This work (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2020-01-27 CP | 88.8 | 40.75 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 2020-07-06 CP | 6.8 | 4.46 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2020-12-23 CP | 19.4 | 8.79 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 2014-09-01 3% | 83.5 | 20.86 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | Scenario400 1% | 66.5 | 25.53 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 2015-01-01 HW | 210.4 | 54.46 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 2015-04-01 LW | 411.6 | 58.75 |

## Effect of the reserve equation

This is the decision that matters most. Equation (67) as printed has no renewable term, so thermal capacity alone must cover load plus reserve. The default model adds the renewable output to the left side. `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.

| Instance | LP, as printed | MIP, as printed | MIP bound | Time (s) | Nodes | MIP change from default |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2886327.663320 | 2895818.506145 | 2895818.506145 | 5.11 | 1 | +135.3% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 4738304.251865 | 4744049.174369 | 4743596.078260 | 118.32 | 57703 | +27.2% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 3420212.426006 | 3427596.725367 | 3427511.589515 | 6.67 | 1 | +26.6% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48408.252585 | 48404.447154 | 19.46 | 1 | none (no renewables) |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 59131.628059 | 59294.766885 | 59289.559388 | 96.74 | 1959 | +76.5% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 70787813.609122 | 70853552.802373 | 70846642.488301 | 77.85 | 1 | +70.8% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57415416.765581 | 57424327.867364 | 57422963.483430 | 103.42 | 1 | +0.7% |

All of these reached the 0.01% gap. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, the printed form uses only 57746 of the 148361 MWh of renewable energy (61% curtailed, against 14% by default), with no reserve shortfall: it curtails free energy to keep thermal units committed.

## Checks

The objective of each solution was not recomputed by separate code. The tools written for that could not be run in this environment; see "Verification" in `NOTES.md`.

**Comparison with an unstrengthened model.** `--variant base` replaces T's generation limits, ramping and piecewise bounds with the basic physical constraints (18), (19), (24), (25), (42). It has the same integer feasible set if T's strengthening is valid, so each model's objective should lie above the other's bound.

| Instance | T objective | T bound | Base objective | Base bound | Consistent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 1230475.366858 | 1230372.814177 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 3729194.920899 | 3728823.125816 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 2707458.250828 | 2707196.479605 | yes |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 48407.906437 | 48404.148645 | yes |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 33590.159078 | 33587.075872 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 41483616.907983 | 41482325.156730 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 57004338.160063 | 56999545.483832 | yes |

This test has limits. It cannot see an error smaller than the gap, which is about $300 on the RTS instances and $5000 on FERC. The two models also share the objective, the up/down-time rows and the start-up rows, so it says nothing about errors in those.

**Hand checks on `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06`, period 18.**
- Thermal output 4861.93 MW plus renewable 1269.30 MW equals demand 6131.23 MW.
- Headroom on the units with spare capacity sums to 183.9369 MW, which equals the reserve requirement.
- Unit `101_STEAM_3` starts at 30 MW with `RU`=`RD`=40. Its `p(1)`=70 is exactly `p0+RU`, and its availability at t=9 is exactly `p(8)+RU`. Its largest drop, 28.71 MW, is within `RD`.

**File format.** On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the MIP CSV has 74 rows for period 1: 73 generators and `RENEWABLE`.

**Independent review.** A separate agent compared `src/model.c` and `src/instance.c` with the paper by reading and hand derivation, without running anything. It found no defect in the default model, and its hand examples support each departure from the printed text.

**Command line.** A 1 s limit on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` returned status `TIME_LIMIT`, an incumbent and `bound=-inf`. A non-JSON input gave a parse error and exit code 1.

# Instance file format

Each file in `data/` is a JSON object describing one unit commitment instance.
Power is in MW, time in hourly periods, and costs in dollars.

## Top level

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `time_periods` | Number of periods in the planning horizon, T |
| `demand` | Array of length T: system load in each period |
| `reserves` | Array of length T: spinning reserve requirement in each period |
| `thermal_generators` | Object mapping each generator's name to its data |
| `renewable_generators` | Object mapping each renewable generator's name to its data |

The instances have no transmission network.

## Each thermal generator

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The generator's name |
| `must_run` | 1 if the generator must be on in every period, otherwise 0 |
| `power_output_minimum`, `power_output_maximum` | Minimum and maximum output when on |
| `ramp_up_limit`, `ramp_down_limit` | Ramp-up and ramp-down rates, per period |
| `ramp_startup_limit`, `ramp_shutdown_limit` | Start-up and shut-down rates |
| `time_up_minimum`, `time_down_minimum` | Minimum up time and minimum down time, in periods |
| `unit_on_t0` | 1 if the generator is on in period 0, otherwise 0 |
| `power_output_t0` | Output in period 0 |
| `time_up_t0`, `time_down_t0` | Number of periods the generator has been on, or off, as of period 0 |
| `startup` | Array of `{lag, cost}`, ordered by increasing `lag`: the start-up cost `cost` applies when the generator has been off for at least `lag` periods |
| `piecewise_production` | Array of `{mw, cost}`, ordered by increasing `mw`: the points of the piecewise linear production cost curve, where `cost` is the hourly cost of producing `mw` |

## Each renewable generator

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The generator's name |
| `power_output_minimum`, `power_output_maximum` | Arrays of length T: minimum and maximum output in each period |

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18)
project(uc_solve C)

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()
add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra)

# Gurobi: $GUROBI_HOME if set, otherwise the install location of this project.
if(DEFINED ENV{GUROBI_HOME})
  set(GUROBI_HOME "$ENV{GUROBI_HOME}")
else()
  set(GUROBI_HOME "/home/dlw/software/gurobi1302/linux64")
endif()
find_path(GUROBI_INCLUDE_DIR gurobi_c.h HINTS "${GUROBI_HOME}/include" REQUIRED)
find_library(GUROBI_LIBRARY NAMES gurobi130 HINTS "${GUROBI_HOME}/lib" REQUIRED)
get_filename_component(GUROBI_LIB_DIR "${GUROBI_LIBRARY}" DIRECTORY)

# Instance handling needs no solver; the verifier and data checker use only this.
add_library(uc_data STATIC src/json.c src/instance.c)
target_include_directories(uc_data PUBLIC src)
target_link_libraries(uc_data PUBLIC m)

add_library(uc_model STATIC src/model.c)
target_include_directories(uc_model PUBLIC src ${GUROBI_INCLUDE_DIR})
target_link_libraries(uc_model PUBLIC uc_data ${GUROBI_LIBRARY})

add_executable(uc_solve src/main.c)
target_link_libraries(uc_solve PRIVATE uc_model)

# Checking tools (see NOTES.md). Neither is needed to solve an instance.
add_executable(uc_verify tools/verify_solution.c)
target_link_libraries(uc_verify PRIVATE uc_data)

add_executable(uc_unitcheck tools/unitcheck.c)
target_link_libraries(uc_unitcheck PRIVATE uc_model)

set_target_properties(uc_solve uc_unitcheck PROPERTIES
  BUILD_RPATH "${GUROBI_LIB_DIR}"
  INSTALL_RPATH "${GUROBI_LIB_DIR}")

# Results: formulation T on the seven instances

All seven MIPs reached the 0.01% gap well inside the 600 s limit, and all seven LP relaxations solved to optimality.

The model departs from the paper's printed text in a few places. One of them, the renewable term in the reserve row (67), changes the objective by up to 135%. See [Effect of the reserve equation](#effect-of-the-reserve-equation) and `NOTES.md`.

## Main results

Objectives are in dollars. Times are Gurobi's reported runtime and exclude reading the file and building the model. "Root gap" is (MIP objective − LP objective) / MIP objective.

| Instance | LP objective | LP time (s) | MIP objective | MIP bound | Gap | MIP time (s) | Nodes | Status | Root gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 0.60 | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 0.0055% | 40.75 | 20366 | OPTIMAL | 0.31% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 0.38 | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 0.0099% | 4.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.18% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2697031.224634 | 0.52 | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 0.0092% | 8.79 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.39% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 6.30 | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 0.0096% | 20.86 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 6.10 | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 0.0100% | 25.53 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 26.02 | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 0.0018% | 54.46 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 21.64 | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 0.0026% | 58.75 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |

OPTIMAL here means within the 0.01% gap, not proved exactly optimal.

Load shed, over-generation and reserve shortfall were zero in every MIP and LP solution above.

| Instance | Renewable used (MWh) | Available (MWh) | Variables | Binaries | Constraints | Nonzeros |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 127873.596 | 148361.000 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 78694.790 | 78711.600 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 80719.254 | 86297.500 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0.000 | 0.000 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 647317.506 | 647317.506 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 1989211.583 | 2106677.220 | 371631 | 181359 | 506007 | 2298488 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 123146.177 | 123146.177 | 378916 | 187252 | 536643 | 2375635 |

Solution files are in `results/`: `<instance>.mip.csv` and `<instance>.lp.csv`. In an LP file, `on` is `u` rounded to 0 or 1 while `power` and `available` use the fractional `u`.

### Setup

- Gurobi 13.0.2, with defaults except `MIPGap=0.0001` and `TimeLimit=600`.
- AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8 cores and 16 threads, 14 GB of RAM. Gurobi used up to 16 threads.
- The solves ran one at a time, with no other solver running.

The commands, for each instance, were:

```
build/uc_solve --relax --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.lp.csv data/NAME.json
build/uc_solve --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.mip.csv --log results/NAME.mip.log data/NAME.json
```

The `.mip.log` files were appended to by more than one run, so each holds several solves. Runs of the same model gave the same objective, bound and node count. The LP `.lp.log` files come from an earlier pass that gave the same objectives.

The binary changed once after these runs, and only in how it prints a bound that is still infinite. `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` was rerun on the last binary as a check.

## Comparison with the paper

The paper reports no objective values, so only solve times can be compared. Its T times come from supplement Tables 17 to 19, on Gurobi 8.0.1 and a Xeon E5-2670. A different solver version and machine make the absolute times incomparable.

| Instance | Paper's name for it | Paper T (s) | This work (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2020-01-27 CP | 88.8 | 40.75 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 2020-07-06 CP | 6.8 | 4.46 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2020-12-23 CP | 19.4 | 8.79 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 2014-09-01 3% | 83.5 | 20.86 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | Scenario400 1% | 66.5 | 25.53 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 2015-01-01 HW | 210.4 | 54.46 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 2015-04-01 LW | 411.6 | 58.75 |

## Effect of the reserve equation

This is the decision that matters most. Equation (67) as printed has no renewable term, so thermal capacity alone must cover load plus reserve. The default model adds the renewable output to the left side. `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.

| Instance | LP, as printed | MIP, as printed | MIP bound | Time (s) | Nodes | MIP change from default |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2886327.663320 | 2895818.506145 | 2895818.506145 | 5.11 | 1 | +135.3% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 4738304.251865 | 4744049.174369 | 4743596.078260 | 118.32 | 57703 | +27.2% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 3420212.426006 | 3427596.725367 | 3427511.589515 | 6.67 | 1 | +26.6% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48408.252585 | 48404.447154 | 19.46 | 1 | none (no renewables) |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 59131.628059 | 59294.766885 | 59289.559388 | 96.74 | 1959 | +76.5% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 70787813.609122 | 70853552.802373 | 70846642.488301 | 77.85 | 1 | +70.8% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57415416.765581 | 57424327.867364 | 57422963.483430 | 103.42 | 1 | +0.7% |

All of these reached the 0.01% gap. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, the printed form uses only 57746 of the 148361 MWh of renewable energy (61% curtailed, against 14% by default), with no reserve shortfall: it curtails free energy to keep thermal units committed.

## Checks

The objective of each solution was not recomputed by separate code. The tools written for that could not be run in this environment; see "Verification" in `NOTES.md`.

**Comparison with an unstrengthened model.** `--variant base` replaces T's generation limits, ramping and piecewise bounds with the basic physical constraints (18), (19), (24), (25), (42). It has the same integer feasible set if T's strengthening is valid, so each model's objective should lie above the other's bound.

| Instance | T objective | T bound | Base objective | Base bound | Consistent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 1230475.366858 | 1230372.814177 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 3729194.920899 | 3728823.125816 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 2707458.250828 | 2707196.479605 | yes |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 48407.906437 | 48404.148645 | yes |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 33590.159078 | 33587.075872 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 41483616.907983 | 41482325.156730 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 57004338.160063 | 56999545.483832 | yes |

This test has limits. It cannot see an error smaller than the gap, which is about $300 on the RTS instances and $5000 on FERC. The two models also share the objective, the up/down-time rows and the start-up rows, so it says nothing about errors in those.

**Hand checks on `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06`, period 18.**
- Thermal output 4861.93 MW plus renewable 1269.30 MW equals demand 6131.23 MW.
- Headroom on the units with spare capacity sums to 183.9369 MW, which equals the reserve requirement.
- Unit `101_STEAM_3` starts at 30 MW with `RU`=`RD`=40. Its `p(1)`=70 is exactly `p0+RU`, and its availability at t=9 is exactly `p(8)+RU`. Its largest drop, 28.71 MW, is within `RD`.

**File format.** On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the MIP CSV has 74 rows for period 1: 73 generators and `RENEWABLE`.

**Independent review.** A separate agent compared `src/model.c` and `src/instance.c` with the paper by reading and hand derivation, without running anything. It found no defect in the default model, and its hand examples support each departure from the printed text.

**Command line.** A 1 s limit on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` returned status `TIME_LIMIT`, an incumbent and `bound=-inf`. A non-JSON input gave a parse error and exit code 1.

# Results: formulation T on the seven instances

All seven MIPs reached the 0.01% gap well inside the 600 s limit, and all seven LP relaxations solved to optimality.

The model departs from the paper's printed text in a few places. One of them, the renewable term in the reserve row (67), changes the objective by up to 135%. See [Effect of the reserve equation](#effect-of-the-reserve-equation) and `NOTES.md`.

These results are from the rebuild after `REFINEMENT_REPORT.md`. **The review changed nothing in the default model**, so the objectives, bounds, node counts and model sizes are the same as in the previous round; only the times differ slightly. See [Comparison with the reference](#comparison-with-the-reference).

## Main results

Objectives are in dollars. Times are Gurobi's reported runtime and exclude reading the file and building the model. "Root gap" is (MIP objective − LP objective) / MIP objective.

| Instance | LP objective | LP time (s) | MIP objective | MIP bound | Gap | MIP time (s) | Nodes | Status | Root gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 0.71 | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 0.0055% | 39.38 | 20366 | OPTIMAL | 0.31% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 0.37 | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 0.0099% | 4.25 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.18% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2697031.224634 | 0.39 | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 0.0092% | 8.56 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.39% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 6.37 | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 0.0096% | 20.56 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 6.02 | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 0.0100% | 25.23 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 25.55 | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 0.0018% | 53.95 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 21.41 | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 0.0026% | 57.85 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |

OPTIMAL here means within the 0.01% gap, not proved exactly optimal.

Load shed, over-generation and reserve shortfall were zero in every MIP and LP solution above.

| Instance | Renewable used (MWh) | Available (MWh) | Variables | Binaries | Constraints | Nonzeros |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 127873.596 | 148361.000 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 78694.790 | 78711.600 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 80719.254 | 86297.500 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0.000 | 0.000 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 647317.506 | 647317.506 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 1989211.583 | 2106677.220 | 371631 | 181359 | 506007 | 2298488 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 123146.177 | 123146.177 | 378916 | 187252 | 536643 | 2375635 |

Solution files are in `results/`: `<instance>.mip.csv` and `<instance>.lp.csv`. In an LP file, `on` is `u` rounded to 0 or 1 while `power` and `available` use the fractional `u`.

### Setup

- Gurobi 13.0.2, with defaults except `MIPGap=0.0001` and `TimeLimit=600`.
- AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8 cores and 16 threads, 14 GB of RAM. Gurobi used up to 16 threads.
- The solves ran one at a time, with no other solver running.

The commands, for each instance, were:

```
build/uc_solve --relax --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.lp.csv data/NAME.json
build/uc_solve --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.mip.csv --log results/NAME.mip.log data/NAME.json
```

The `.mip.log` files were appended to by more than one run, so each holds several solves. Runs of the same model gave the same objective, bound and node count. The LP `.lp.log` files come from an earlier pass that gave the same objectives.

The binary changed once after these runs, and only in how it prints a bound that is still infinite. `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` was rerun on the last binary as a check.

## Comparison with the paper

The paper reports no objective values, so only solve times can be compared. Its T times come from supplement Tables 17 to 19, on Gurobi 8.0.1 and a Xeon E5-2670. A different solver version and machine make the absolute times incomparable.

| Instance | Paper's name for it | Paper T (s) | This work (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2020-01-27 CP | 88.8 | 40.75 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 2020-07-06 CP | 6.8 | 4.46 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2020-12-23 CP | 19.4 | 8.79 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 2014-09-01 3% | 83.5 | 20.86 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | Scenario400 1% | 66.5 | 25.53 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 2015-01-01 HW | 210.4 | 54.46 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 2015-04-01 LW | 411.6 | 58.75 |

## Effect of the reserve equation

This is the decision that matters most. Equation (67) as printed has no renewable term, so thermal capacity alone must cover load plus reserve. The default model adds the renewable output to the left side. `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.

| Instance | LP, as printed | MIP, as printed | MIP bound | Time (s) | Nodes | MIP change from default |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2886327.663320 | 2895818.506145 | 2895818.506145 | 5.11 | 1 | +135.3% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 4738304.251865 | 4744049.174369 | 4743596.078260 | 118.32 | 57703 | +27.2% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 3420212.426006 | 3427596.725367 | 3427511.589515 | 6.67 | 1 | +26.6% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48408.252585 | 48404.447154 | 19.46 | 1 | none (no renewables) |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 59131.628059 | 59294.766885 | 59289.559388 | 96.74 | 1959 | +76.5% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 70787813.609122 | 70853552.802373 | 70846642.488301 | 77.85 | 1 | +70.8% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57415416.765581 | 57424327.867364 | 57422963.483430 | 103.42 | 1 | +0.7% |

All of these reached the 0.01% gap. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, the printed form uses only 57746 of the 148361 MWh of renewable energy (61% curtailed, against 14% by default), with no reserve shortfall: it curtails free energy to keep thermal units committed.

## Checks

The objective of each solution was not recomputed by separate code. The tools written for that could not be run in this environment; see "Verification" in `NOTES.md`.

**Comparison with an unstrengthened model.** `--variant base` replaces T's generation limits, ramping and piecewise bounds with the basic physical constraints (18), (19), (24), (25), (42). It has the same integer feasible set if T's strengthening is valid, so each model's objective should lie above the other's bound.

| Instance | T objective | T bound | Base objective | Base bound | Consistent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 1230475.366858 | 1230372.814177 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 3729194.920899 | 3728823.125816 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 2707458.250828 | 2707196.479605 | yes |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 48407.906437 | 48404.148645 | yes |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 33590.159078 | 33587.075872 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 41483616.907983 | 41482325.156730 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 57004338.160063 | 56999545.483832 | yes |

This test has limits. It cannot see an error smaller than the gap, which is about $300 on the RTS instances and $5000 on FERC. The two models also share the objective, the up/down-time rows and the start-up rows, so it says nothing about errors in those.

**Hand checks on `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06`, period 18.**
- Thermal output 4861.93 MW plus renewable 1269.30 MW equals demand 6131.23 MW.
- Headroom on the units with spare capacity sums to 183.9369 MW, which equals the reserve requirement.
- Unit `101_STEAM_3` starts at 30 MW with `RU`=`RD`=40. Its `p(1)`=70 is exactly `p0+RU`, and its availability at t=9 is exactly `p(8)+RU`. Its largest drop, 28.71 MW, is within `RD`.

**File format.** On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the MIP CSV has 74 rows for period 1: 73 generators and `RENEWABLE`.

**Independent review.** A separate agent compared `src/model.c` and `src/instance.c` with the paper by reading and hand derivation, without running anything. It found no defect in the default model, and its hand examples support each departure from the printed text.

**Command line.** A 1 s limit on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` returned status `TIME_LIMIT`, an incumbent and `bound=-inf`. A non-JSON input gave a parse error and exit code 1.

# Results: formulation T on the seven instances

All seven MIPs reached the 0.01% gap well inside the 600 s limit, and all seven LP relaxations solved to optimality.

The model departs from the paper's printed text in a few places. One of them, the renewable term in the reserve row (67), changes the objective by up to 135%. See [Effect of the reserve equation](#effect-of-the-reserve-equation) and `NOTES.md`.

These results are from the rebuild after `REFINEMENT_REPORT.md`. **The review changed nothing in the default model**, so the objectives, bounds, node counts and model sizes are the same as in the previous round; only the times differ slightly. See [Comparison with the reference](#comparison-with-the-reference).

## Main results

Objectives are in dollars. Times are Gurobi's reported runtime and exclude reading the file and building the model. "Root gap" is (MIP objective − LP objective) / MIP objective.

| Instance | LP objective | LP time (s) | MIP objective | MIP bound | Gap | MIP time (s) | Nodes | Status | Root gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 0.71 | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 0.0055% | 39.38 | 20366 | OPTIMAL | 0.31% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 0.37 | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 0.0099% | 4.25 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.18% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2697031.224634 | 0.39 | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 0.0092% | 8.56 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.39% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 6.37 | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 0.0096% | 20.56 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 6.02 | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 0.0100% | 25.23 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.02% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 25.55 | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 0.0018% | 53.95 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 21.41 | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 0.0026% | 57.85 | 1 | OPTIMAL | 0.01% |

OPTIMAL here means within the 0.01% gap, not proved exactly optimal.

Load shed, over-generation and reserve shortfall were zero in every MIP and LP solution above.

| Instance | Renewable used (MWh) | Available (MWh) | Variables | Binaries | Constraints | Nonzeros |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 127873.596 | 148361.000 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 78694.790 | 78711.600 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 80719.254 | 86297.500 | 39137 | 21425 | 44488 | 206976 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0.000 | 0.000 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 647317.506 | 647317.506 | 228176 | 127280 | 453078 | 1245007 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 1989211.583 | 2106677.220 | 371631 | 181359 | 506007 | 2298488 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 123146.177 | 123146.177 | 378916 | 187252 | 536643 | 2375635 |

Solution files are in `results/`: `<instance>.mip.csv` and `<instance>.lp.csv`. In an LP file, `on` is `u` rounded to 0 or 1 while `power` and `available` use the fractional `u`.

### Setup

- Gurobi 13.0.2, with defaults except `MIPGap=0.0001` and `TimeLimit=600`.
- AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8 cores and 16 threads, 14 GB of RAM. Gurobi used up to 16 threads.
- The solves ran one at a time, with no other solver running.

The commands, for each instance, were:

```
build/uc_solve --relax --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.lp.csv data/NAME.json
build/uc_solve --time-limit 600 --solution results/NAME.mip.csv --log results/NAME.mip.log data/NAME.json
```

All 14 solves above ran on the final binary. The `.mip.log` files are appended to on each run, so each holds several solves, with this round's last. Runs of the same model gave the same objective, bound and node count. The LP `.lp.log` files come from an earlier pass that gave the same objectives.

## Comparison with the reference

`REFINEMENT_REPORT.md` compares the program with a reference implementation. Both solved to a 0.01% gap. `NOTES.md` has the reasoning for each conclusion.

**LP.** Six of the seven agree to six decimals. On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the program's LP is higher by 108.857. This traces to one row, (35) at t=1: the program uses the printed form, and the reference behaves as a weaker form of that row with the same integer solutions. `--variant first-ramp-u0` solves the weaker form, and gives the reference's LP on all seven:

| Instance | LP, default | LP, `first-ramp-u0` | LP, reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1226645.339956 | 1226645.339956 | 1226645.339956 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3722397.471090 | 3722397.471090 | 3722397.471090 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | **2697031.224634** | 2696922.367712 | 2696922.367712 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48399.526919 | 48399.526919 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33585.584391 | 33585.584391 | 33585.584391 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41480391.463026 | 41480391.463026 | 41480391.463026 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 56994290.752337 | 56994290.752337 | 56994290.752337 |

That the reference uses this form is an inference from these values; I have not seen its code. The default remains the printed row, which is valid and tighter.

**MIP.** All intervals overlap, and each objective difference is below the 0.01% gap. The largest relative difference is 0.0074%, on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw`. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` and `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` the objectives are identical.

On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23`, a zero-gap solve gives 2707458.250827 with the default model and 2707458.250828 with the weaker row. That value lies inside both reported intervals, and equals the objective of the basic model below. These two solves used a temporary gap override that is not in the delivered program.

**Independent check.** The one failure, on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw`, is rounding in the six-decimal CSV, not a violated constraint. It will still appear if the check is rerun with the same tolerance, because neither the solution nor the format changed.

| Instance | Row in the solver: largest shortfall | `s_R` | Worst `R - sum(available - power)` from values rounded to six decimals | Periods above 1e-5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 4.5e-12 | 0 | 2.8e-14 | 0 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 9.1e-13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 9.1e-13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 4.4e-11 | 0 | 8.0e-6 | 0 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 1.0e-10 | 0 | **1.1e-5 (t=7)** | **1** |

These figures came from temporary instrumentation, since removed. The last two columns can be recomputed from the `.mip.csv` files.

## Comparison with the paper

The paper reports no objective values, so only solve times can be compared. Its T times come from supplement Tables 17 to 19, on Gurobi 8.0.1 and a Xeon E5-2670. A different solver version and machine make the absolute times incomparable.

| Instance | Paper's name for it | Paper T (s) | This work (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2020-01-27 CP | 88.8 | 40.75 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 2020-07-06 CP | 6.8 | 4.46 |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2020-12-23 CP | 19.4 | 8.79 |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 2014-09-01 3% | 83.5 | 20.86 |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | Scenario400 1% | 66.5 | 25.53 |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 2015-01-01 HW | 210.4 | 54.46 |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 2015-04-01 LW | 411.6 | 58.75 |

## Effect of the reserve equation

This is the decision that matters most. Equation (67) as printed has no renewable term, so thermal capacity alone must cover load plus reserve. The default model adds the renewable output to the left side. `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.

| Instance | LP, as printed | MIP, as printed | MIP bound | Time (s) | Nodes | MIP change from default |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 2886327.663320 | 2895818.506145 | 2895818.506145 | 5.11 | 1 | +135.3% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 4738304.251865 | 4744049.174369 | 4743596.078260 | 118.32 | 57703 | +27.2% |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 3420212.426006 | 3427596.725367 | 3427511.589515 | 6.67 | 1 | +26.6% |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48399.526919 | 48408.252585 | 48404.447154 | 19.46 | 1 | none (no renewables) |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 59131.628059 | 59294.766885 | 59289.559388 | 96.74 | 1959 | +76.5% |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 70787813.609122 | 70853552.802373 | 70846642.488301 | 77.85 | 1 | +70.8% |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57415416.765581 | 57424327.867364 | 57422963.483430 | 103.42 | 1 | +0.7% |

All of these reached the 0.01% gap. On `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, the printed form uses only 57746 of the 148361 MWh of renewable energy (61% curtailed, against 14% by default), with no reserve shortfall: it curtails free energy to keep thermal units committed.

## Checks

The objective of each solution was not recomputed by separate code. The tools written for that could not be run in this environment; see "Verification" in `NOTES.md`.

**Comparison with an unstrengthened model.** `--variant base` replaces T's generation limits, ramping and piecewise bounds with the basic physical constraints (18), (19), (24), (25), (42). It has the same integer feasible set if T's strengthening is valid, so each model's objective should lie above the other's bound.

| Instance | T objective | T bound | Base objective | Base bound | Consistent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27` | 1230475.366858 | 1230407.984483 | 1230475.366858 | 1230372.814177 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06` | 3729194.920899 | 3728825.770989 | 3729194.920899 | 3728823.125816 | yes |
| `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | 2707509.117416 | 2707260.274187 | 2707458.250828 | 2707196.479605 | yes |
| `ca_2014-09-01_reserves_3` | 48409.123688 | 48404.470950 | 48407.906437 | 48404.148645 | yes |
| `ca_Scenario400_reserves_1` | 33590.742186 | 33587.387286 | 33590.159078 | 33587.075872 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` | 41483157.102869 | 41482399.553225 | 41483616.907983 | 41482325.156730 | yes |
| `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | 57001082.949048 | 56999603.005677 | 57004338.160063 | 56999545.483832 | yes |

This test has limits. It cannot see an error smaller than the gap, which is about $300 on the RTS instances and $5000 on FERC. The two models also share the objective, the up/down-time rows and the start-up rows, so it says nothing about errors in those.

**Hand checks on `rts_gmlc_2020-07-06`, period 18.**
- Thermal output 4861.93 MW plus renewable 1269.30 MW equals demand 6131.23 MW.
- Headroom on the units with spare capacity sums to 183.9369 MW, which equals the reserve requirement.
- Unit `101_STEAM_3` starts at 30 MW with `RU`=`RD`=40. Its `p(1)`=70 is exactly `p0+RU`, and its availability at t=9 is exactly `p(8)+RU`. Its largest drop, 28.71 MW, is within `RD`.

**File format.** On `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` the MIP CSV has 74 rows for period 1: 73 generators and `RENEWABLE`.

**Independent review.** A separate agent compared `src/model.c` and `src/instance.c` with the paper by reading and hand derivation, without running anything. It found no defect in the default model, and its hand examples support each departure from the printed text.

**Command line.** A 1 s limit on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` returned status `TIME_LIMIT`, an incumbent and `bound=-inf`. A non-JSON input gave a parse error and exit code 1.

Because of the same restriction, the data checks that I first wrote as a separate tool became the `data warning` lines in `uc_solve`. A solver should report these anyway, but it is also why they live there.

The paper's reference implementation (EGRET) and the benchmark library were not consulted, as instructed.

## Refinement round: `REFINEMENT_REPORT.md`

**Outcome.** I found no error in the model, so the default model is unchanged. Its objectives, bounds and node counts on all seven instances are the same as before. If the check is rerun with the same tolerance, it will report the same reserve line, for the reason in item 3.

| Item in the report | Conclusion | Changed | Reason, in brief |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. LP differs on `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` | Acceptable. The program matches the printed row. | Default model: nothing. Added `--variant first-ramp-u0`. | One row, (35) at t=1, explains the difference. The printed form is valid and tighter, and has the same integer solutions. |
| 2. LPs agree on the other six | Correct | Nothing | They also support departures 1 and 2 above. |
| 3. MIP objectives and bounds differ; all intervals overlap | Acceptable | Nothing | Each difference is below the 0.01% gap. |
| 4. Reserve "violated" once by 0.000011 on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | Not a violation by the model. Six-decimal rounding in the CSV. | Nothing | The row holds to 1.0e-10 in the solver. The check's figure is reproduced exactly from the rounded values. |

### Item 1: LP on `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23`

The program gives 2697031.224634 and the reference 2696922.367712. The program is higher by 108.857, so it is the tighter one here. That is what a row cutting off feasible points would look like, so I tested for that first.

**Cause.** (35) at t=1 reads `p̄'(1) - p'(0) <= (SU-P_) v(1) - RU v(1) + RU u(1)`. By (2), `u(1) - v(1) = u(0) - w(1)`, so this is

`p̄'(1) <= p'(0) + (SU-P_) v(1) + RU (u(0) - w(1))`.

Leaving out the `-RU w(1)` gives a weaker row, with `RU u(0)` in its place. `--variant first-ramp-u0` solves that form.

**Evidence.**
- With the weaker row, the December LP is 2696922.367712, equal to the reference in all six decimals.
- The other six LPs do not move, and all equal the reference. So this one row accounts for all seven LP values.
- The closest other candidates did not match. Examples are (24) at t=1 (2696909.55), and availability at t=1 freed on the 76 MW units only (2696922.96).

That the reference uses this form is an inference from these values. I have not seen its code, and other forms could give the same values.

**Why only this instance.** The weaker row only matters if some `w(1)` is above zero and availability at t=1 has value. The reserve row's dual at t=1 is 2.93 on December and 0 on January and July. Load falls in December's first hours, and the LP partly shuts down on-units: `323_CC_2` and `313_CC_1` are fractional at t=1. The LP solutions on the CAISO and FERC instances did not change either.

**Why this is not an error.**
- *The program matches the paper.* Table 3 lists (35), with no exception for t=1, and `p'(0)` is defined from the data.
- *The row is valid at t=1.* If `u(0)=u(1)=1`, it says `p̄'(1) <= p'(0)+RU`. If the unit shuts down at 1, then `u(1)=0` and `p̄'(1)=0`, while the right side is `p'(0) >= 0`. A start at 1 gives `p̄'(1) <= SU-P_`.
- *Both forms have the same integer solutions.* When `w(1)=0` the two rows are identical. When `w(1)=1`, (38) or (23) already forces `p̄'(1)=0`, so neither row binds. A spurious `v(1)=w(1)=1` is excluded as in departure 2.
- *The optimum agrees.* At zero gap, December gives 2707458.250827 with the printed row and 2707458.250828 with the weaker one. The basic model reached the same objective in the previous round. The value lies inside both MIP intervals in the report, so the printed row did not cut off the reference's solution, whose objective is 2707468.09.

Changing the default would make the model weaker and less faithful to the printed row, solely to match a number. I did not do that.

**What this does not show.** The zero-gap solve tests one objective on one instance. It is not a proof that T is valid in general. The per-generator test that would be stronger, `uc_unitcheck`, still could not be run.

### Item 2: the six LPs that agree

They agree to six decimals, which is good evidence that the two models match on the rows that bind there. They also bear on two earlier decisions:
- **Departure 1, renewable term in (67).** The reference's LP is 1226645.34 on `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`, equal to the default model; the printed form gives 2886327.66. The check also treats the requirement as one that these solutions meet. So the reference and the check both agree with this reading. That is corroboration, and still not a statement from the paper, so it remains your decision.
- **Departure 2, clamped rows for UT or DT above T.** The reference's LP on `ferc_2015-01-01_hw` is 41480391.46, equal to the default model; the rows as printed give 36213647.

Agreement says nothing about rows that do not bind in any of these LPs, such as the extra term of (41) or departure 5, which has no effect when SU=SD.

### Item 3: MIP objectives and bounds

All seven intervals overlap, and both programs stopped at a 0.01% gap. The objective differences are 0 on two RTS days, and otherwise from 0.00025% (`ferc_2015-01-01_hw`) to 0.0074% (`ferc_2015-04-01_lw`), all below the gap. Where the two differ, they are different points within the tolerance, reached by different search paths. On `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` the program's objective is the lower of the two.

### Item 4: reserve on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw`

**Cause.** Rounding when the solution is written to six decimals.

**Evidence, from the same solution as the report** (same objective and bound):
- In the solver's values, the reserve row's largest shortfall is 1.0e-10, `s_R` is 0 in every period, and every `u` is exactly 0 or 1. So rounding `u` in the writer plays no part.
- From values rounded as in the CSV, `R - sum(available - power)` has a worst value of 1.100e-05, at t=7. Exactly one period is above 1e-5. That matches the report's "1 times, worst excess 0.000011".
- The same calculation puts no period above 1e-5 on the other six instances, which also matches the report. The next largest is 8.0e-6 on `ferc_2015-01-01_hw`.

So the check appears to test `sum(available - power) >= R` with a tolerance of 1e-5. This is an inference from the match. The other form, `sum available + renewable >= D + R`, has a worst value of 7.0e-6 on the same data, and does not exceed 1e-5.

**Why nothing was changed.** The format is fixed at six decimals, and no model change affects this. Each of the 978 generators contributes two rounded values, so rounding alone can reach `2 x 978 x 5e-7`, about 9.8e-4, against the check's 1e-5. Biasing the rounding in the writer would remove the line without correcting anything, and would disturb the power balance. A tolerance of about 1e-3 on this sum would be appropriate for a CSV at this precision, or the check could use more digits if the format ever allows.

### How this was measured

- **Finding the row.** I temporarily instrumented `uc_solve` to drop row families by period and generator, print duals on the system rows, change the penalties and start-up category boundaries, override the gap, and print reserve residuals. All of that has been removed. Only `first-ramp-u0` remains.
- **Reproducible with the delivered program:** the LP values in `RESULTS.md`, including those with `first-ramp-u0`.
- **Not reproducible without that instrumentation:** the zero-gap solves, the duals and the solver-side residuals. The rounded residuals can be recomputed from `results/*.mip.csv`.
- **The reference's numbers were used only as a target for diagnosis.** No model change was made to match them.

### Not run

`build/uc_verify` and `build/uc_unitcheck` were denied again, so **they have still never been executed**, and the commands under "Verification" remain the way to run them. I did not add their function to `uc_solve` to get around that. The new variant was built with the rest but not tested under `uc_unitcheck`.

The tables in `RESULTS.md` for the printed reserve form and the basic model, and the hand checks, are from the previous round and were not rerun.

- In the solver's values, the reserve row's largest shortfall is 1.0e-10, `s_R` is 0 in every period, and every `u` is exactly 0 or 1. So rounding `u` in the writer plays no part.
- From values rounded as in the CSV, `R - sum(available - power)` has a worst value of 1.100e-05, at t=7. Exactly one period is above 1e-5. That matches the report's "1 times, worst excess 0.000011".
- The same calculation puts no period above 1e-5 on the other six instances, which also matches the report. The next largest is 8.0e-6 on `ferc_2015-01-01_hw`.

So the check appears to test `sum(available - power) >= R` with a tolerance of 1e-5. This is an inference from the match. The other form, `sum available + renewable >= D + R`, has a worst value of 7.0e-6 on the same data, and does not exceed 1e-5.

**Why nothing was changed.** The format is fixed at six decimals, and no model change affects this. Each of the 978 generators contributes two rounded values, so rounding alone can reach `2 x 978 x 5e-7`, about 9.8e-4, against the check's 1e-5. Biasing the rounding in the writer would remove the line without correcting anything, and would disturb the power balance. A tolerance of about 1e-3 on this sum would be appropriate for a CSV at this precision, or the check could use more digits if the format ever allows.

### How this was measured

- **Finding the row.** I temporarily instrumented `uc_solve` to drop row families by period and generator, print duals on the system rows, change the penalties and start-up category boundaries, override the gap, and print reserve residuals. All of that has been removed. Only `first-ramp-u0` remains.
- **Reproducible with the delivered program:** the LP values in `RESULTS.md`, including those with `first-ramp-u0`.
- **Not reproducible without that instrumentation:** the zero-gap solves, the duals and the solver-side residuals. The rounded residuals can be recomputed from `results/*.mip.csv`.
- **The reference's numbers were used only as a target for diagnosis.** No model change was made to match them.

### Not run

`build/uc_verify` and `build/uc_unitcheck` were denied again, so **they have still never been executed**, and the commands under "Verification" remain the way to run them. I did not add their function to `uc_solve` to get around that. The new variant was built with the rest but not tested under `uc_unitcheck`.

The tables in `RESULTS.md` for the printed reserve form and the basic model, and the hand checks, are from the previous round and were not rerun.

content.text:
I found no error in the model, so the default model is unchanged and its objectives, bounds and node counts are the same as last round. The program is rebuilt, all seven instances are rerun (LP and MIP, 600 s limit), and `RESULTS.md` and `NOTES.md` are updated.

**If you rerun the check with the same tolerance, it will report the same reserve line.** I concluded this line is a rounding artefact in the output, so I left it alone.

## What each item means

| Report item | Conclusion | Why |
|---|---|---|
| LP differs on `rts_gmlc_2020-12-23` (program higher by 108.857) | Acceptable | The difference comes from one row, (35) at t=1. The program uses the printed row, which is valid and tighter. |
| LP agrees on the other six | Correct | This also supports two earlier departures from the paper: the renewable term in (67) and the clamped up/down-time rows. |
| MIP objectives and bounds differ | Acceptable | All intervals overlap and every difference is below the 0.01% gap; the largest is 0.0074%. |
| Reserve "violated" by 0.000011 on `ferc_2015-04-01_lw` | Not a model violation | It comes from rounding the CSV to six decimals. The solver's own row holds to 1.0e-10. |

## Evidence
- **LP:** By (2), the printed row at t=1 contains a `−RU·w(1)` term. Removing that term gives the reference's December LP exactly (2696922.367712) and leaves the other six unchanged, so one row accounts for all seven values.
- **Same integer solutions:** I showed algebraically that the two forms allow the same integer solutions. On December, both solve at zero gap to 2707458.2508.
- **Why only December:** the reserve row at t=1 binds only there among the three RTS days, because the LP partly shuts down units as load falls in the first hours.
- **Reserve:** computing `R − Σ(available − power)` from values rounded to six decimals gives 1.100e-05 at t=7. Exactly one period exceeds 1e-5, and only on this instance, which matches the report. With 978 generators, rounding alone can reach about 1e-3, so a tolerance near that would suit this sum.

## What changed
- **New option:** `--variant first-ramp-u0` lets you reproduce the LP finding. The command line form and output formats are otherwise as before.
- **Notes:** `NOTES.md` has a new section for this round, and now records the penalty values `C_LP`=10000 and `C_RP`=1000. The paper and data give no values for these, and the notes had never mentioned them. They don't affect any objective here because the slacks are zero.

## Limits of this work
- **Inferences:** I inferred the reference's row and the check's reserve formula from matching numbers; I haven't seen either one's code.
- **Blocked tools:** `uc_verify` and `uc_unitcheck` were denied again, so neither has ever been run, and I did not build their function into `uc_solve` to get around that. The zero-gap agreement covers one objective on one instance, so it doesn't prove T valid in general; `uc_unitcheck` would be the stronger test.
- **Temporary instrumentation:** the zero-gap solves, duals and solver-side residuals came from temporary code in `uc_solve`, now removed, so the delivered program can't reproduce them. The LP values can be reproduced, and the rounded residuals can be recomputed from `results/*.mip.csv`.
- **Not rerun:** the `RESULTS.md` tables for the printed reserve form and the basic model, and the hand checks, are from the previous round.

## Decision for you
The renewable term in (67) is still a departure from the printed equation. The reference now agrees with it, for example an LP of 1226645 against 2886328 for the printed form on `rts_gmlc_2020-01-27`. That supports the reading but doesn't come from the paper, so whether to keep it remains your call. I kept it; `--variant reserve-printed` solves the printed form.
